$description: Structured representation of Contera's agent capability model, governance/permission model, risk model, Experience Constitution (Rules 001-011), and the registry of unresolved policy questions. Derived from context/product.md Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9. Non-authoritative — see context/manifest.md §7.

agent_capability_tiers.note: Capability describes what the Operations Agent is technically/product-wise capable of. Capability does not determine whether the agent is permitted to perform the action autonomously — see governance_outcomes.

tiers.name: Observe
tiers.description: identify, classify, compare, summarize, or structure information without committing a consequential change to product or world state

tiers.name: Recommend
tiers.description: suggest an action or next step but does not prepare or execute the action

tiers.name: Prepare
tiers.description: assemble the information or artifact needed for an action but does not commit the consequential action itself

tiers.name: Execute
tiers.description: commits an action that changes product or world state

governance_outcomes.note: Agent capability and governance are separate dimensions (product.md §4.1). Observe->Recommend->Prepare->Execute->Escalate is explicitly NOT one linear authority ladder (invalidated by Scenario 002).

outcomes.name: Permitted
outcomes.description: The action may proceed under the current actor's authority and applicable product rules.

outcomes.name: ApprovalRequired
outcomes.description: An authorized human must review and explicitly approve the prepared action before execution.

outcomes.name: EscalationRequired
outcomes.description: The situation or proposed action must be reviewed by a specific role or higher-authority actor before proceeding.

outcomes.name: Prohibited
outcomes.description: The actor is not allowed to perform the action under the applicable product policy.

governance_outcomes.note_on_unresolved: context/components.md adds a fifth literal, 'UNRESOLVED', to its GovernanceOutcome type for cases where governance policy for an action type has not been decided. This is not a fifth conceptual outcome defined in product.md itself; it is components.md's explicit representation of the absence of one of the four above. See components.md, PreparedActionStatus 'blockedByUnresolvedPolicy'.

risk_model.note: Helps the team reason about appropriate agent autonomy and human intervention. Does not independently determine product policy.

consequence.question: How harmful would an incorrect action or conclusion be?

levels.Low: negligible customer, operational, financial, legal, or safety harm
levels.Moderate: meaningful customer friction, operational disruption, or financial loss
levels.High: substantial financial, customer, legal, safety, or business harm

consequence.note: Consequence is severity, not probability. A low-probability event may still have High consequence.

irreversibility.question: How difficult would the outcome be to undo?

levels.Low: easily undone with little residual effect
levels.Moderate: can be undone, but requires meaningful effort or leaves consequences after reversal
levels.High: cannot practically be undone, or creates lasting consequences even if a formal reversal is possible

illustrative_examples_not_final_policy: sending an SMS: potentially Moderate because it cannot literally be unsent
charging a credit card: potentially Moderate because it can be refunded but customer impact may remain
making a consequential external accusation/report: potentially High

evidentiary_uncertainty.question: How well does available evidence support the system's understanding or proposed action?

levels.Low: relevant facts are available, consistent, and sufficiently reliable
levels.Moderate: some information is missing, ambiguous, inferred, or conflicting, but a reasonable conclusion may still be possible
levels.High: critical evidence is missing, unreliable, or contradictory enough that a consequential conclusion cannot safely be reached

evidentiary_uncertainty.note: Distinguishes human certainty from evidentiary certainty.

time_sensitivity.question: How quickly must intervention occur to prevent or materially reduce the potential consequence?

levels.Low: delay is unlikely to materially change the outcome
levels.Moderate: action is required within a meaningful operational window
levels.High: delay could imminently create or materially increase harm

time_sensitivity.note: Emerged from Scenario 003; related to, but distinct from, potential impact.

probability_likelihood.note: The team explicitly separated probability from consequence but has not determined whether probability should be a first-class risk dimension, how it should be calculated, or whether it should be surfaced to users.

experience_rules.title: Resolve material uncertainty before consequential action
experience_rules.text: When missing or conflicting information could materially change a consequential outcome, seek the strongest available evidence before recommending or executing that outcome.

experience_rules.title: Separate potential impact from intervention urgency
experience_rules.text: Potential consequence and required intervention timing are independent dimensions. Do not use one generic severity value to represent both.

experience_rules.title: Prefer inspectable evidence over opaque confidence
experience_rules.text: When practical, expose the observations, evidence, limitations, and assumptions supporting an AI inference rather than relying on an unexplained numerical confidence score.

experience_rules.title: Reduce autonomy as consequence and irreversibility increase
experience_rules.text: Agent authority should consider the potential impact of an incorrect action and how easily that action can be reversed. Directional, not a complete decision algorithm.

experience_rules.title: Preserve the distinction between observation, inference, recommendation, and human decision
experience_rules.text: The system must not collapse different epistemic stages into a stronger claim than the evidence supports.

experience_rules.title: Apply asymmetric thresholds to high-consequence uncertainty
experience_rules.text: When plausible outcomes have materially different severity, the evidentiary threshold for proceeding should reflect the more consequential failure mode.

experience_rules.title: When AI introduces friction, help resolve the consequences
experience_rules.text: If the system blocks, delays, or escalates an action, it should proactively identify safe paths forward where possible rather than merely stopping the user.

experience_rules.title: Do not substitute assumptions for missing product policy
experience_rules.text: When required product behavior, policy, permissions, evidence, or domain information is undefined, the system must identify the gap and request human resolution rather than silently inventing a rule. Applies both to AI inside Contera and to AI assisting the product team in maintaining Contera's specification.

experience_rules.title: Revalidate mutable state before consequential execution
experience_rules.text: An agent must confirm that the facts and conditions supporting a prepared action remain valid immediately before execution when relevant state may have changed. Establishes the general principle only; per-action fields to revalidate are defined per action as they arise.

experience_rules.title: Prioritize interventions according to urgency and consequence
experience_rules.text: Intelligent interventions should be placed according to the urgency and consequence of the user decision, not merely according to the information architecture of the underlying data. Use the least interruptive treatment sufficient for the intervention window and potential consequence.

experience_rules.title: Use progressive disclosure to minimize decision burden
experience_rules.text: Show only the information necessary to understand the situation and make the immediate decision. Supporting evidence, reasoning, provenance, uncertainty details, and prepared-action metadata should remain inspectable when relevant but need not be simultaneously visible.

permitted: prepare supporting evidence and a draft damage report
prohibited: autonomously assess or collect the proposed ~$1,250-$1,700 damage charge in Scenario 002
